data.description:
## Context / Problem

`next_batch` returns a ticket as available for work while `ticket_deps` reports that same
ticket has open blockers and `ready_to_work: false`. The two readiness answers disagree, and
`next_batch` is the one agents are told to use to pick work, so an agent following it can
claim a ticket whose prerequisites have not landed.

## Reproduction

Observed 2026-09-01 on the live store, epic `spin-cub-usher` (`65dd-e93b-666a-4caa`).

The epic's ADR child `eaved-lighted-hedgehog` (`a5bf-c1f8-3950-4f87`) was linked with two
prerequisite edges recorded from the prerequisite side:

```
link modern-loathful-snake        eaved-lighted-hedgehog blocks
link divinatory-offensive-groundhog eaved-lighted-hedgehog blocks
```

Both prerequisites are open. Then:

- `ticket_deps eaved-lighted-hedgehog` returns
  `{"deps": [], "blockers": ["1cef-7fbc-e402-467c", "5169-ab69-9c23-4f8b"], "ready_to_work": false}`
- `next_batch spin-cub-usher` returns that same `a5bf-c1f8-3950-4f87` inside `batch`, with
  `available_pool: 2`, and does not list it under any `skipped_*` key.

Expected: a ticket with an open blocker is excluded from `batch` (it belongs in a skipped
bucket). Actual: it is offered as available work.

## Root cause

`src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py` derives readiness solely from a ticket's OUTGOING
`depends_on` relations. At `next_batch.py:176-182` it builds `open_depends_on` by filtering
that ticket's own `deps` for `relation == "depends_on"` and skips the ticket only when that
list is non-empty; the blocked-id set at `next_batch.py:220-228` applies the same
outgoing-`depends_on` test.

A `blocks` edge recorded from the prerequisite (`A blocks B`) leaves B with an INBOUND edge
and no outgoing `depends_on`, so B passes both filters. `ticket_deps` computes `blockers`
from the inbound direction and therefore disagrees.

This matters because both link directions are sanctioned: `AGENTS.md` documents `blocks` and
`depends_on` as two of the canonical relations, and the brainstorm/authoring guidance tells
authors to "record their parent and prerequisite relationships with `blocks` or
`depends_on`". Only one of those two spellings is honored by the scheduler.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py` readiness derivation, plus its tests. The fix is to
treat an open inbound `blocks` edge as blocking, exactly as `ticket_deps` already does — not
to change the link vocabulary or the recorded edges.

## Non-goals

- Changing `ticket_deps`, which is the surface that already answers correctly.
- Altering blocking-link promotion or the link relation vocabulary.
- Reworking the file-impact conflict scheduling in the same module.

## Compatibility and rollback

Behavior-narrowing: tickets that were previously offered while blocked stop being offered.
No stored data or event shape changes, so back-out is reverting the readiness predicate.
Any consumer relying on the current over-permissive batch would have been scheduling
unclaimable work.

## Testing

Unit tests against the real `next_batch_state` over a temporary store seeded with a
prerequisite pair, covering both edge spellings and the symmetry with `ticket_deps`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ticket whose only prerequisite edge is an inbound `blocks` from an OPEN ticket is
      absent from `batch` and present in a skipped bucket; verified by `pytest` over a
      seeded temporary store asserting the returned `batch` ids.
- [ ] The same ticket becomes available once that prerequisite closes; verified by `pytest`
      asserting it appears in `batch` after the blocker transitions to closed.
- [ ] `next_batch` and `ticket_deps` agree for every child of a seeded epic: no id appears in
      `batch` while `ticket_deps` reports `ready_to_work: false`; verified by `pytest`
      asserting the intersection is empty.
- [ ] The existing outgoing-`depends_on` behavior is unchanged; verified by `pytest` over a
      seeded pair using `depends_on`, asserting the same exclusion as before.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the live reproduction above no longer
offers `a5bf-c1f8-3950-4f87` while its blockers are open.
data.title: next_batch schedules a blocked ticket: readiness ignores inbound blocks edges
